hints: Look at the shape of the energy profile, it has two humps with a valley at Z, so think about what type of substitution this suggests.
Notice the starting haloalkane is tertiary, the C-Cl carbon is joined to three other carbons, so the C-Cl bond can break first on its own to give a stable intermediate.
At point Z the chloride ion has already left but hydroxide has not yet joined, so work out the charge left on that carbon with only three bonds.
walkthrough:
**Identify the type of haloalkane**

This is a tertiary chloroalkane. The carbon bonded to Cl is also bonded to one $\text{CH}_3$ group and two ring $\text{CH}_2$ groups, so three carbons in total. Tertiary haloalkanes favour $\text{S}_{\text{N}}1$ hydrolysis.

$$\text{(CH}_3\text{)(C}_6\text{H}_{10}\text{)C-Cl = tertiary}$$

**Read the energy profile**

The profile shows two peaks with a dip at Z. That means two steps with an intermediate in the middle. This is the classic $\text{S}_{\text{N}}1$ pathway: step 1 loses $\text{Cl}^-$, step 2 adds $\text{OH}^-$.

$$\text{R-Cl} \rightarrow \text{R}^+ + \text{Cl}^- \text{ then } \text{R}^+ + \text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{R-OH}$$

**Find the charge at Z**

At Z we are in the valley between the steps. The C-Cl bond has broken heterolytically, both electrons went to Cl to make $\text{Cl}^-$. The carbon is left with only three bonds and six outer electrons, so it is a carbocation with a full positive charge.

$$\text{charge on C at Z = 1+}$$

options.A: Not correct. A 1- charge would mean the carbon gained an extra electron to become a carbanion. Here the carbon loses $\text{Cl}^-$ and is electron deficient, not electron rich.
options.B: Not correct. $\delta-$ means a small partial negative charge, as in a polarised bond. At Z there is no C-Cl or C-O bond to polarise, the intermediate is a free ion, not a transition state.
options.C: Not correct. $\delta+$ is the partial charge seen in the polar C-Cl bond in the reactant, or in an $\text{S}_{\text{N}}2$ transition state. At Z the bond has fully broken to give a full carbocation, so the charge is larger than $\delta+$.
options.D: Correct. Point Z is the $\text{S}_{\text{N}}1$ carbocation intermediate, $\text{(CH}_3\text{)(C}_6\text{H}_{10}\text{)C}^+$. The tertiary carbon has three bonds and a full 1+ charge after losing $\text{Cl}^-$.
